definitions.explanation: Attached to the masu-stem of a verb to mean 'way of doing.' Functions as a suffix in this usage.
A polite way to refer to a person. More respectful than 人.

examples.japanese: この{漢字|かんじ}の{読|よ}み{方|かた}は？
examples.english: How do you read this kanji?

examples.japanese: {箸|はし}の{持|も}ち{方|かた}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.english: Please teach me how to hold chopsticks.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}の{作|つく}り{方|かた}を{母|はは}から{習|なら}った。
examples.english: I learned how to cook from my mother.

examples.japanese: あの{方|かた}はどなたですか。
お{客|きゃく}さまの{中|なか}に、お{医者|いしゃ}さまの{方|かた}はいらっしゃいますか。
examples.english: Is there a doctor among the passengers?

examples.japanese: こちらの{方|かた}が{担当|たんとう}の{田中|たなか}さんです。
examples.english: This is Mr. Tanaka, the person in charge.

notes:
SENSE 1 — WAY OF DOING:
Attaches to the masu-stem of verbs: {verb stem}+{方|かた}.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {読|よ}み{方|かた}: way of reading
- {書|か}き{方|かた}: way of writing
- {使|つか}い{方|かた}: way of using
- {食|た}べ{方|かた}: way of eating
- {考|かんが}え{方|かた}: way of thinking

SENSE 2 — PERSON (POLITE):
More polite than {人|ひと}. Used in formal speech and polite conversation. Often preceded by あの, この, その, or どの.

NOTE: {方|かた} (person) is distinct from {方|ほう} (direction/alternative), which is a separate word with the same kanji.
